name: Decode Base64
description: Standard Base64 decode. Look for A–Z, a–z, 0–9, +, / with = padding.

name: Decode Base64 (URL-safe)
description: URL-safe Base64 variant using - and _ instead of + and /. Common in JWTs and web apps.

name: Double Base64 Decode
description: Decode data that has been Base64-encoded twice — a common CTF obfuscation layer.

name: Decode Hex
description: Decode hex-encoded data. Auto-detects space, colon, 0x-prefix, or no delimiter.

name: Decode Binary
description: Decode space-separated binary (0s and 1s) to ASCII text.

name: Decode Octal
description: Decode space-separated octal values to ASCII text.

name: Decode Decimal / Char Codes
description: Decode space-separated decimal character codes (e.g. 72 101 108 108 111) to ASCII text.

name: URL Decode
description: Decode percent-encoded URL characters (%20 → space, %3D → =, etc.).

name: HTML Entity Decode
description: Decode HTML entities (& → &, < → <, A → A, etc.).

name: Decode Base32
description: Decode Base32-encoded data (A–Z, 2–7, = padding).

name: Decode Base58
description: Decode Base58 (Bitcoin alphabet — no 0, O, I, l characters).

name: Decode Base85 (Ascii85)
description: Decode Base85 / Ascii85 encoded data.

name: ROT13
description: Rotate letters by 13 positions. Self-inverse — encoding and decoding are the same operation.

name: ROT47
description: Rotate all printable ASCII characters (0x21–0x7e) by 47. Includes digits and symbols.

name: Caesar Brute Force (all 25 shifts)
description: Try every Caesar cipher rotation (1–25) and display each result. Scan for readable plaintext.

name: Atbash Cipher
description: Reverse-alphabet substitution (A↔Z, B↔Y, …). Self-inverse.

name: XOR Brute Force (single byte)
description: Try all 255 single-byte XOR keys and display results. Scan output for readable text.

name: XOR with Known Key (hex)
description: XOR input with a hex key. Edit the key argument (currently 00) before baking.

name: Vigenère Decode
description: Decode a Vigenère cipher with a known key. Edit the key argument (currently KEY) before baking.

name: From Morse Code
description: Decode Morse code to text. Expects dots (.) and dashes (-) separated by spaces, lines by newlines.

name: Bacon Cipher Decode
description: Decode Bacon's cipher — groups of 5 A/B characters encoding letters.

name: A1Z26 Decode
description: Convert numbers to letters (1=A, 2=B, …, 26=Z). Expects space-separated values.

name: MD5 Hash
description: Compute the MD5 hash of the input.

name: SHA-1 Hash
description: Compute the SHA-1 hash of the input.

name: SHA-256 Hash
description: Compute the SHA-256 hash of the input.

name: Identify Hash Type
description: Analyse a hash string to identify its likely algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, bcrypt, NTLM, etc.).

name: Decode JWT
description: Decode a JSON Web Token — splits and Base64-decodes the header, payload, and signature.

name: URL Decode → HTML Entity Decode
description: Double-decode: percent-encoding first, then HTML entities. Common in web challenge payloads.

name: Extract URLs
description: Extract all URLs from the input using regex.

name: Extract Email Addresses
description: Extract all email addresses from the input.

name: Strip HTTP Headers
description: Remove HTTP headers from a raw HTTP response, leaving only the body.

name: Magic — Auto-detect
description: Automatically detect encoding, file type, and language. Suggests the most likely recipe. Start here when you have unknown data.

name: Magic — Intensive (CTF mode)
description: Magic with intensive mode: brute-forces XOR (255 keys), bit rotations, all 25 Caesar shifts, and character encodings. Slower but finds more.

name: Detect File Type
description: Identify the file type by reading magic bytes (file signature). Useful for files with wrong or missing extensions.

name: Entropy Analysis
description: Calculate Shannon entropy. Low (<3.5) = text-like, medium (3.5–6) = encoded/compressed, high (>6) = encrypted or compressed.

name: Extract Printable Strings
description: Extract sequences of printable ASCII characters — like the Unix 'strings' command. Useful for binary/executable analysis.

name: Hex Dump
description: View data as a hex dump with ASCII preview column. Essential for binary analysis.

name: Extract Hashes
description: Extract MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and other hash strings from text.
